item.research_question: How does doping with different Nb contents (0–9 wt%) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and fracture behavior of CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys prepared by high-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering?
item.processing_route: High-energy ball milling (400 rpm, 4 h total with 10 min cooling intervals) followed by discharge plasma sintering (SPS) at 1100 °C, 30 MPa pressure, for 10 min; heating rates: 100 °C/min (0–600 °C), 50 °C/min (600–900 °C), 25 °C/min (900–1100 °C)
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing (cross-sectional area 1.5 mm × 1 mm, tensile rate 0.2 mm/min, original gauge length 5 mm); Vickers hardness (500 g load, 15 s retention); XRD (Cu Kα, 40 kV, 40 mA, 20–90°); SEM/EDS analysis
key_findings: Nb0 alloy has FCC single-phase structure with tensile strength 656.3 MPa, yield strength 269.4 MPa, and elongation 62.2%.
Nb9 alloy reaches maximum tensile strength 893.2 MPa and yield strength 775.4 MPa, but elongation drops to 11.8%.
Nb5 alloy shows optimal balance: tensile strength 879.1 MPa, yield strength 491.8 MPa, and elongation 39.8%.
Hardness increases from 201 HV (Nb0) to 336 HV (Nb9), nearly proportional to Laves phase volume fraction.
Laves phase (Co2Nb-type, HCP) forms with Nb addition; its volume fraction increases with Nb content.
FCC matrix is enriched in Co, Cr, Fe, Ni; Laves phase is enriched in Nb (~35%) and depleted in Cr, Fe, Ni.
Fracture mode shifts from ductile (Nb0–Nb5) to brittle (Nb7–Nb9) as Nb content increases.
item.mechanism: The large atomic size of Nb causes lattice distortion in the FCC matrix (solid solution strengthening), while the formation of hard, brittle Nb-rich Laves phase provides precipitation strengthening; the trade-off between FCC matrix plasticity and Laves phase brittleness determines overall properties.
quotes: The results show that with the addition of the Nb element, the lattice distortion of the alloy due to the large size of the Nb atoms causes the microstructure of CoCrFeNi HEAs to change from a single-phase FCC structure to a dual-phase structure of FCC and Laves.
The Nb5 alloy showed the most excellent comprehensive performance, with a tensile strength, yield strength, and plasticity of 879.1 MPa, 491.8 MPa, and 39.8%, respectively.
The increase in the hardness of the HEAs was nearly proportional to the increase in the volume fraction of the Laves phase, which was the direct cause of the increase in the hardness of the HEA.

records.text: Paper card. Question: How does doping with different Nb contents (0–9 wt%) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and fracture behavior of CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys prepared by high-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering?. System: CoCrFeNi-Nbx (x = 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 wt%) high-entropy alloys. Processing: High-energy ball milling (400 rpm, 4 h total with 10 min cooling intervals) followed by discharge plasma sintering (SPS) at 1100 °C, 30 MPa pressure, for 10 min; heating rates: 100 °C/min (0–600 °C), 50 °C/min (600–900 °C), 25 °C/min (900–1100 °C). Test conditions: Room temperature tensile testing (cross-sectional area 1.5 mm × 1 mm, tensile rate 0.2 mm/min, original gauge length 5 mm); Vickers hardness (500 g load, 15 s retention); XRD (Cu Kα, 40 kV, 40 mA, 20–90°); SEM/EDS analysis. Findings: Nb0 alloy has FCC single-phase structure with tensile strength 656.3 MPa, yield strength 269.4 MPa, and elongation 62.2%.; Nb9 alloy reaches maximum tensile strength 893.2 MPa and yield strength 775.4 MPa, but elongation drops to 11.8%.; Nb5 alloy shows optimal balance: tensile strength 879.1 MPa, yield strength 491.8 MPa, and elongation 39.8%.; Hardness increases from 201 HV (Nb0) to 336 HV (Nb9), nearly proportional to Laves phase volume fraction.; Laves phase (Co2Nb-type, HCP) forms with Nb addition; its volume fraction increases with Nb content.; FCC matrix is enriched in Co, Cr, Fe, Ni; Laves phase is enriched in Nb (~35%) and depleted in Cr, Fe, Ni.; Fracture mode shifts from ductile (Nb0–Nb5) to brittle (Nb7–Nb9) as Nb content increases.. Mechanism: The large atomic size of Nb causes lattice distortion in the FCC matrix (solid solution strengthening), while the formation of hard, brittle Nb-rich Laves phase provides precipitation strengthening; the trade-off between FCC matrix plasticity and Laves phase brittleness determines overall properties.. Quote: "The results show that with the addition of the Nb element, the lattice distortion of the alloy due to the large size of the Nb atoms causes the microstructure of CoCrFeNi HEAs to change from a single-phase FCC structure to a dual-phase structure of FCC and Laves."
